title: Design a Notification Service — Object Model
prompt: Design the object model for a reusable notification service used across a company. It sends notifications over multiple channels (email, SMS, push, in-app), renders content from templates, respects user preferences and opt-outs, and retries transient failures. Design the core classes, the channel and template abstractions, the preference model, and the retry mechanism. Focus on class design and APIs. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: Multi-channel dispatch via Strategy, templated content, preference/opt-out gating, and a retry-with-backoff mechanism.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Separates functional (multi-channel send, templates, preferences, retry, dedupe) from non-functional (extensible channels, at-least-once delivery, no spamming opted-out users).

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Notification, Channel, Template, Recipient, Preference, DeliveryStatus, Provider — cleanly separated.

rubric.label: Class design & responsibilities
rubric.description: Channel is an abstraction over providers; Template rendering separated from sending; preferences gate dispatch.

rubric.label: Relationships & cardinality
rubric.description: Notification targets a Recipient over 1..* Channels; Template per (event, channel); Preference per (user, channel/category). Association reasoned.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: Strategy for channels, Factory for channel/provider selection, Template Method or Builder for rendering, Observer for delivery-status callbacks, Chain/Decorator for the send pipeline.

rubric.label: SOLID / OCP
rubric.description: Adding a new channel (WhatsApp) or provider requires no change to existing dispatch; preference logic isolated (SRP).

rubric.label: API / method design
rubric.description: send(notificationRequest), registerChannel, render(template, data), getStatus, setPreference — clear signatures.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: New channels/providers, batching, scheduling, localization, rate limiting added without core rewrites.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: User opted out of a channel, provider down, template missing/render error, invalid contact info, duplicate suppression, quiet hours.

rubric.label: Concurrency & delivery semantics
rubric.description: At-least-once vs exactly-once, idempotency/dedupe keys, retry backoff, DLQ, worker fan-out.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Narrates the dispatch pipeline and abstractions, states tradeoffs, reasons about delivery guarantees.

functional_requirements: Accept a notification request (event/category, recipient, payload) and deliver it
Support channels: email, SMS, push, in-app — extensible to more
Render content from per-channel templates with variable substitution + localization
Respect user preferences and opt-outs per channel and per category
Retry transient failures with backoff; dead-letter after max attempts
Track and expose delivery status per notification
nonfunctional_requirements: Adding a new channel/provider must not touch existing dispatch code (OCP)
At-least-once delivery with dedupe to avoid duplicate sends
Never send to users who opted out
clarifying_questions: Which channels at launch, and which providers per channel (e.g. SES vs SendGrid)?
Delivery guarantee — at-least-once with dedupe, or best-effort?
Do preferences apply per channel, per category, or both? Are there quiet hours?
Is templating owned by us or provided per event? Do we localize?
Do we batch/digest or send each event immediately?

core_classes.name: NotificationRequest
core_classes.responsibility: Inbound intent: what event, to whom, with what data.

core_classes.name: Notification
core_classes.responsibility: A rendered, channel-specific message ready to dispatch.

core_classes.name: Channel
core_classes.responsibility: Strategy abstraction: send a rendered Notification via its provider(s).

core_classes.name: EmailChannel / SmsChannel / PushChannel / InAppChannel
core_classes.responsibility: Concrete channels wrapping a Provider (SES, Twilio, FCM, DB).

core_classes.name: Provider
core_classes.responsibility: Adapter over an external delivery vendor.

core_classes.name: Template / TemplateEngine
core_classes.responsibility: Per (event, channel, locale) template; renders body from data.

core_classes.name: PreferenceService
core_classes.responsibility: Stores and evaluates per-user opt-in/out by channel and category; quiet hours.

core_classes.name: RetryPolicy
core_classes.responsibility: Decides whether/when to retry a failed send (backoff, max attempts).

core_classes.name: ChannelFactory
core_classes.responsibility: Resolves a ChannelType (and provider) to a Channel instance.

core_classes.name: NotificationService / Dispatcher
core_classes.responsibility: Orchestrates: gate by preferences → render template → select channel → send → apply retry → record status.

relationships: NotificationService depends on Channel, Template, PreferenceService, RetryPolicy abstractions (DIP).
A NotificationRequest fans out to 0..* Notifications (one per allowed channel).
Channel is-a Strategy; each concrete Channel composes a Provider adapter.
Template is keyed by (eventType, channel, locale); TemplateEngine renders it with request data.
PreferenceService gates the fan-out; DeliveryStatus is tracked per Notification.

design_patterns.why: Each channel's send logic varies; new channels plug in without editing the dispatcher (OCP).
Decouples the dispatcher from concrete channel/provider construction and lets provider swap by config.

design_patterns.where: Provider wraps SES/Twilio/FCM SDKs behind a uniform deliver()
design_patterns.why: Isolates third-party vendor APIs from the domain.

design_patterns.where: Provider delivery-status webhooks/callbacks update Notification status
design_patterns.why: Async delivery receipts decouple status tracking from the send call.

design_patterns.where: send pipeline: preference-check → rate-limit → dedupe → render → deliver
design_patterns.why: Cross-cutting stages compose cleanly and are individually testable/toggleable.

state_transitions: Notification: QUEUED → SENDING → SENT → DELIVERED (on provider receipt) | FAILED
FAILED → (RetryPolicy) → RETRYING → SENDING ... until DELIVERED or max attempts → DEAD_LETTER
SUPPRESSED terminal when preferences/opt-out block the send
edge_cases: User opted out of a channel/category → SUPPRESSED, not sent
Provider returns transient 5xx / timeout → retry with backoff; permanent 4xx (invalid number) → no retry, dead-letter
Template missing for (event, channel, locale) → fall back to default locale or fail loudly
Recipient missing contact for a channel (no phone) → skip that channel
Duplicate request (same dedupe key) → suppress the duplicate
Quiet hours → defer delivery to allowed window
Partial fan-out success (email ok, SMS failed) → per-channel status
concurrency: Async workers consume a queue; horizontal scale by partitioning on recipient/notificationId
At-least-once delivery + idempotency/dedupe key so retries don't double-send
RetryPolicy with exponential backoff + jitter; move to DLQ after max attempts
Provider rate limits enforced per-channel (token bucket) to avoid throttling
Delivery receipts arrive out of order via webhooks — update status idempotently
extensibility: New channel (WhatsApp/Slack) → new Channel strategy + register in factory, zero dispatcher changes
New provider for an existing channel → new Adapter, swap by config
Batching/digest → an aggregation stage before dispatch
Scheduling/delay → a scheduler enqueues at time T
Localization → templates keyed by locale; A/B templates by variant

deep_dives.probe: Show the Channel interface and how you'd add WhatsApp without touching the dispatcher. Where does provider selection (SES vs SendGrid for email) live?
Preferences apply per channel and per category, plus global opt-out and quiet hours. Where in the pipeline is this evaluated, and how do you keep that logic out of every channel?
A send times out. How do you decide to retry, how do you back off, and how do you avoid double-sending on retry? What lands in the dead-letter queue?
Providers report delivery asynchronously via webhooks that can arrive out of order or twice. How do you track final status correctly?
How are templates organized across events, channels, and locales, and what happens when one is missing?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions channel or email or sms or push
followup_bank.question: Add WhatsApp as a channel. How much existing code changes? If the dispatcher changes, your design isn't open/closed.

followup_bank.trigger: mentions preference or opt-out or unsubscribe
followup_bank.question: Where do you evaluate opt-outs and quiet hours so the rule isn't duplicated in every channel?
Which failures do you retry vs dead-letter, and how do you back off? How do retries avoid sending the same message twice?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions provider or vendor or twilio or ses
followup_bank.question: How do you swap the email provider from SES to SendGrid without touching the dispatcher?
How are templates keyed across event, channel, and locale, and what's the fallback when one is missing?

tradeoffs: At-least-once + dedupe (simple, robust) vs exactly-once (expensive, often illusory)
Synchronous send (simple, blocks caller) vs async queue (scalable, eventual)
One channel per strategy (clean OCP) vs a parameterized sender (fewer classes, poor extensibility)
Pipeline as Chain of Responsibility (composable stages) vs a hardcoded method (simpler, rigid)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer makes Channel a Strategy behind a ChannelFactory with per-channel Provider adapters (Adapter pattern) so new channels/providers obey OCP, and structures dispatch as a pipeline (Chain of Responsibility): preference/opt-out gate → dedupe/rate-limit → template render → deliver → status. Preferences and quiet hours live in one PreferenceService evaluated once, not scattered across channels. It defines at-least-once delivery with an idempotency key so retries don't double-send, a RetryPolicy with exponential backoff + jitter and a dead-letter queue for exhausted/permanent failures, and updates delivery status idempotently from out-of-order provider webhooks. Signal: 'add WhatsApp with zero dispatcher changes' and a concrete retry/dedupe story.

interviewer_notes: Let them scope channels and delivery guarantee. The core signal is Channel-as-Strategy behind a factory — test with 'add WhatsApp without touching the dispatcher.' Push on where preference/opt-out logic lives; a weak answer sprinkles it into every channel, a strong one gates once in the pipeline. Force the retry conversation: which errors retry vs dead-letter, backoff, and how idempotency stops double-sends. If they claim exactly-once, probe how. Delivery-status via async webhooks (out-of-order/duplicate) is a good stretch. Keep it object-design focused.
